{"cc":[{"text":"Patient presents with new onset right second toe pain over the past five days. He also has a chronic painful callus on the same foot's plantar third metatarsal head that is due for paring.","start_char":54,"end_char":211}],"hpi":[{"text":"43-year-old male, recreational runner, presents with five days of right second toe pain. Pain began after a 12-mile training run. Localized to the second toe, worse with push-off during gait, mild swelling noted, no significant ecchymosis. He denies a specific acute injury but recalls feeling a "twinge" toward the end of the run. He has continued running but at reduced volume. He is also due for paring of his chronic painful intractable plantar keratoma at the right plantar third metatarsal head, last debrided four months ago.","start_char":221,"end_char":563}],"exam_findings":[{"text":"Right foot second toe: tenderness localized to the second metatarsophalangeal joint dorsal aspect, mild dorsal-plantar swelling, no obvious deformity. Lachman test of the MTP joint reveals subtle plantar plate laxity compared to the contralateral side. Range of motion limited by pain at end-range plantarflexion. No skin breakdown. Right plantar third metatarsal head: discrete intractable plantar keratoma, 7mm diameter, central nucleation, surrounding hyperkeratosis. No ulceration. Both feet otherwise: pulses +2, no other lesions, neurovascular intact.","start_char":576,"end_char":1008}],"mdm":[{"text":"Right second MTP plantar plate strain suspected based on history and Lachman positivity. Recommend paring of the keratoma today. Patient consents to the paring procedure.","start_char":1029,"end_char":1154}],"procedure_note":[{"text":"Following informed consent: right plantar third metatarsal head intractable keratoma was pared using sterile technique. No bleeding.","start_char":1166,"end_char":1264}],"ambiguous_segments":[{"text":"Plan:
- Routine paring complete, return in 4 months
- Return PRN for any concerns","start_char":1265,"end_char":1329},{"text":"WHY THIS IS A MIXED-CRITERION CASE:

Distinct CC: PASS. The second toe pain is wholly distinct from the callus paring indication.

Separate exam: PASS. The MTP exam (Lachman test, dorsal swelling, range of motion) is independent of the callus exam. Two different anatomic structures examined with different techniques.

Independent MDM: FAIL. Despite the strong CC and exam, the MDM collapses. There is one sentence acknowledging plantar plate strain "recommend paring of the keratoma today" jumps directly to the procedure with no plan for the second toe at all. No imaging considered, no taping or buddy-strapping discussed, no activity modification, no follow-up criteria, no NSAID, no differential discussion. The MDM does not establish independent decision-making for the plantar plate problem.

Site-specificity: N/A (same foot).

This case is diagnostically valuable because it tests whether the analyzer correctly scores criteria independently. If the system scores PASS on all three based on the strong CC and exam, it has not actually applied the four-criterion rubric, it has averaged. If it correctly scores FAIL on independent_mdm despite the PASS on the other two, the criterion-by-criterion architecture is working as designed.

The Drafter should produce remediation specifically targeting the MDM, not the CC or exam. If the Drafter produces remediation for all three criteria, it's pattern-matching rather than reading the actual scores.","start_char":1330,"end_char":2035}]}
